findings.who: A filer whose margin or investment loan is in the name of a revocable living trust, an intentionally defective grantor trust, or a single-member LLC that holds only investments. The interest is reported to the filer on a grantor letter or brokerage statement, not on a Schedule K-1.
findings.why_no: The entity bullet names only 'a partnership or an S corporation'. The filer reads 'Did you or your spouse pay' as excluding interest the trust or LLC paid on its own account.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Investment interest expense is interest paid or accrued on a loan or part of a loan that is allocable to property held for investment"
findings.fix: Add a bullet: 'interest paid by a grantor trust (including a revocable living trust) or a single-member LLC you own, on a loan used for investments'.

findings.who: A filer who borrowed more than $10,000 interest-free or below market from a relative and invested the money. Section 7872 treats the forgone interest as paid by the borrower.
findings.why_no: No interest was actually paid or charged, so 'pay or accrue any interest' is answered no.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Enter the investment interest expense paid or accrued during the tax year, regardless of when you incurred the indebtedness"
findings.fix: Add a bullet: 'a below-market or interest-free loan of over $10,000 used for investments (imputed interest may apply)'.

findings.who: A filer with a short stock sale held open more than 45 days who paid the lender amounts in lieu of dividends. Pub. 550 can treat those payments as investment interest.
findings.why_no: The payments are not interest on 'money borrowed'. The filer borrowed shares, not money.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Purpose of Form: "For more information, see Pub. 550, Investment Income and Expenses"
findings.fix: Add a bullet: 'payments in lieu of dividends on a short sale'. Classify the amount in a later question.
